title: 2026 NFL Trade Deadline Live Updates: Rumors, Buzz & Deals in Final Two Days – CBS Sports
body:
The NFL trade deadline looms, and General Managers are once again glued to their phones, weighing options and negotiating deals before the clock strikes 4 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday, Nov. 10. With just two days left in the 2024‑25 season, a flurry of rumors has already surfaced, ranging from blockbuster quarterback swaps to strategic depth‑chart upgrades. While some franchises have already sealed deals, many remain on the fence, hoping to capitalize on emerging injury reports and the shifting playoff picture.

One of the most talked‑about possibilities involves the Denver Broncos, who are reportedly courting the Miami Dolphins’ veteran quarterback. Denver’s current starter has struggled with consistency, and the Broncos’ front office is eager to add a proven passer to revive a stagnant offense. Miami, on the other hand, is rumored to be seeking draft capital and a defensive lineman to bolster a unit that has underperformed in recent weeks. A trade would give both clubs a fresh start, but the price tag—potentially a first‑round pick and a mid‑season drafter—has sparked debate among analysts about whether the gamble is worth the risk.

In the NFC, the Dallas Cowboys are believed to be exploring a trade for a versatile edge rusher from the Seattle Seahawks. Dallas’ defensive line has been plagued by injuries, and the Cowboys’ scouting department has identified the Seahawks’ player as a perfect fit for their 3‑4 scheme. Seattle, meanwhile, is looking to offload salary and acquire a young safety and a third‑round pick. The deal could reshape both defenses, yet the Cowboys must navigate salary‑cap constraints and the Seahawks’ reluctance to part with a player who has been a key contributor.

The New England Patriots have quietly entered the market for a reliable slot receiver, targeting a third‑year wideout from the Detroit Lions who has shown flashes of playmaking ability but has been limited by inconsistent quarterback play. New England’s passing attack has lacked a true possession receiver, and the addition could provide a crucial missing piece as the Patriots push for a postseason berth. Detroit, meanwhile, is looking to add a veteran linebacker and a late‑round draft pick, hoping to reinforce a defense that has struggled to stop the run.

On the opposite side of the ledger, the Jacksonville Jaguars appear content to sit out the deadline, focusing instead on internal development. Their recent acquisition of a veteran cornerback from the Chicago Bears has already paid dividends, and the Jaguars’ front office has signaled that they prefer to preserve draft capital for the upcoming 2026 draft rather than engage in a costly mid‑season swap. This conservative approach underscores a growing trend among smaller‑market teams that prioritize long‑term building over immediate, high‑priced fixes.

Meanwhile, the league’s trade chatter has been amplified by a spate of injury updates. A star running back from the Los Angeles Rams suffered a high‑ankle sprain, prompting the Rams to explore backup options through the waiver wire rather than a trade. Similarly, a starting linebacker for the Green Bay Packers is listed as questionable, leading to speculation that the Packers might seek a short‑term solution via a trade for a veteran special‑teams ace. These injury‑driven narratives add urgency to the negotiations, as clubs weigh the cost of a potential trade against the risk of missing the playoffs.

As the deadline approaches, the NFL landscape could shift dramatically. Teams that successfully navigate the market stand to gain a competitive edge, while those that miss out may find themselves scrambling in the final weeks of the season. With the playoffs just weeks away, every roster move will be scrutinized, and the outcomes of these negotiations will likely reverberate well beyond the regular season. The next 48 hours promise a cascade of announcements, and fans should brace for a final round of high‑stakes maneuvering that could reshape the postseason picture.
